title: Reverse Psychology
idea: Brief #32. Angle swap of our launched winner #160 (Johnny / Max, skin tags, "Do not buy Haven & Spool until you hear..."): same hook, same numbered countdown and "here's the lie" offer reveal, swapped to wrinkles / under-eyes, the angle with enemies (Botox, lotions) and a mechanism (soaks in vs sits on top) as concrete as skin tags. Enemy + mechanism per point = the #1 pattern in 100 winning scripts.

script.script: Do not buy Haven & Spool until you hear what they didn't tell you about the results.
script.visual: Initial image (like #160): woman, 50, at her vanity, holding the amber bottle up next to her face, serious look, forehead lines and crow's feet visible. Alt: close-up of the rose quartz roller gliding beside her eye, then she looks into the camera. Alt: her finger pointing at the camera, bottle in the other hand.
script.on_screen_text: Do not buy Haven & Spool (same as #160)

script.script: Number one, it softens the look of wrinkles with immense hydration. Wrinkles aren't just age.
script.visual: Big "1"; tight close-ups of forehead lines, crow's feet and the lines between the brows (woman 50 to 60, real skin texture); quick cut of her looking at her lines in the mirror, unimpressed.

script.script: They're thin skin that dried out and lost its moisture. And modern lotion just sits on top.
script.visual: Extreme macro of thin skin drying out in time-lapse: the surface dulls, tightens and crinkles into fine lines. Then a hand rubs a thick white modern lotion over that same dry, crinkled skin: it smears and sits on top as a white film; the lines stay exactly the same underneath.

script.script: Cold-pressed castor oil soaks in and holds that moisture there all night, so your skin looks smoother and plumper by morning. No botox, no expensive lotions.
script.visual: Same patch of skin: the rose quartz roller rolls golden castor oil over it; the oil sinks in, the skin visibly hydrates and plumps, the fine lines soften (slow, satisfying, macro). Woman waking up touching her cheek in soft morning light. A syringe and a row of pricey lotion jars pushed aside, then our single amber bottle.

script.script: Number two, it actually soaks in. Modern creams and lotions only sit on the surface. That's why the lines are still there every morning.
script.visual: Big "2"; side-by-side macro on two patches of skin: left = white lotion still sitting on top, shiny and filmy after a minute; right = castor oil fully absorbed (optional 3D skin cross-section, like #129). Woman frowning at her lines in the bathroom mirror, coffee in hand.

script.script: Haven & Spool's 90% ricinoleic acid soaks in instead of sitting on top. When your skin stays hydrated all night, the wrinkles disappear
script.visual: Macro of a golden oil drop on the rose quartz ball, then rolling it under her eye; same woman in morning light touching the corner of her eye, smiling.

script.script: Number three, it's third-party tested. Organic. Hexane-free. Cold-pressed to keep the ricinoleic acid alive. No fillers. No synthetic chemicals. No plastic packaging that leaches into the oil. What's on the label is what's in the bottle.
script.visual: Big "3"; castor beans, oil going from the press into amber glass, macro of our label, a plastic bottle crossed out on "no plastic packaging".

script.script: Number four, and here's the lie. We said we couldn't do better than 50% off. We were wrong. Right now, you can buy one and get one free. That's two bottles of Haven & Spool for the price of one. And once this batch sells out, it's going back to full price.
script.visual: Big "4"; back to her on camera, smirking; two bottles on the counter.

script.script: Now you know. You're a few clicks away from smoother-looking skin without Botox, without spending more on lotions, and getting two bottles for the price of one. Click the link below before we sell out.
script.visual: She holds both bottles up, points down.

editing_notes: Replicate our winner #160 exactly (same structure, hook, numbered countdown ending on "Number four, and here's the lie", same pacing), only the angle swapped from skin tags to wrinkles / under-eyes. Reference link = the original Facebook ad Johnny modeled. Johnny's Haven & Spool recreation (watch this first, it's the winner): https://hyperscale.ceo/briefs/8650493d-8e3f-4c19-999f-36b37cb61054 . Copy his version with our new angle on top. Each numbered point: big number on screen (1, 2, 3, 4) + B-roll that shows exactly what she's saying. Key demo: thin skin drying and crinkling → white modern lotion sits on top, lines unchanged → castor oil sinks in, skin hydrates and plumps. Claims: look/feel only (smoother-looking, plumper-looking). Doc: Brief H+S, tab #32.

Voiceover: American accent female, 50, her own voice: confident, a little conspiratorial on "here's the lie". NEEDS TO HAVE CONVICTION in their voice, it's boring to listen to a dull script. They need to speak with character.

Avatar: Same format as our launched winner #160 (Johnny / Max, skin tags): a 50-year-old woman, real-looking (real skin texture, light makeup), at her bathroom vanity. On camera ONLY for the hook and number four (the lie); everything else is B-roll over her voice (very little talking head). Visible forehead lines, crow's feet and some under-eye puffiness. Product aware.
